answers.explanation: Still taking orders at half speed during an attack counts as robust.
Closing known holes keeps the system working under attack. The second connection is redundancy, and recovery time is a rapidity metric.
User awareness, along with alerting people when an attack is going around, is part of robustness.
A low count might mean strong defenses or blind sensors. The metric can't tell the difference by itself.
It's about focusing limited people, money, and equipment on what matters most.
Using external expertise is one way to mobilize resources you don't have in-house.
Prioritized functionality: everyone knows the order before the incident starts.
Multi-purpose people and technology give you options when something fails.
Choosing what to save first is prioritizing resources.
